caption: A pan of rice left on the stove boils dry, and smoke begins to rise as the grains on the bottom scorch black.

sa.check: A pan of rice sits on a stove.
The steam gives way to thin smoke.
The smoke rises from the pan.
The grains on the bottom blacken.
The blackening spreads from the bottom.
The steam comes first and the smoke follows.

pc.expect: The change runs one way: steam gives way to smoke as the last water goes, the smoke thickens and the blackening only spreads.
pc.fail: The smoke gives way back to steam with the pan still on the heat; or a blackened grain turns white again; or the blackening spreads and then shrinks; or the water returns to the pan and the rice steams again.

pc.expect: The blackening happens in the rice at the pan's bottom and spreads from there, while the rice above stays paler.
pc.fail: The rice at the top blackens while the grains on the pan's bottom stay white; or the pan's outside changes colour rather than the rice; or the whole panful blackens at once with no spreading; or the rice blackens before any steam has gone.

pc.expect: The smoke rises out of the pan, spreading and thinning.
pc.fail: The smoke pours down the pan's sides and pools on the hob; or sinks below the pan; or hangs as a fixed shape without rising; or pours downward through the pan's base.

pc.expect: The smoke comes from the scorching rice at the pan's bottom and appears only once the water has gone.
pc.fail: Thick smoke pours from the pan while water still stands in it and steam is rising; or the smoke comes from the hob beside the pan; or the rice blackens while no smoke leaves the pan at all.

pc.expect: One pan of rice; the rice stays in the pan and its level only drops as the water goes.
pc.fail: The rice's level rises with nothing added; or rice appears outside the pan with none leaving it; or a second pan appears; or rice passes through the pan's base.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The pan's outside, the hob and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The pan changes colour; or its handle changes shape; or items around the hob rearrange.

note: The scorching of the rice is the caption's asserted outcome; the chemistry of it is not judged, only that the darkening runs one way and starts at the pan's bottom.
